## About
The Synapse Visual Studio Code extension supports a pro-developer experience for exploring Microsoft Fabric lakehouses, and authoring Fabric notebooks and Spark job definitions. Learn more about the extension, including how to get started with the necessary prerequisites.

Visual Studio (VS) Code is a one of the most popular lightweight source code editors; it runs on your desktop and is available for Windows, macOS, and Linux. By installing the Synapse VS Code extension, you can author, run, and debug your notebook and Spark job definition locally in VS Code. You can also post the code to the remote Spark compute in your Fabric workspace to run or debug. The extension also allows you to browse your lakehouse data, including tables and raw files, in VS Code.

## Featured Tags

- `v2.0.6`

 ```docker pull mcr.microsoft.com/msfabric/synapsevscode/fabric-synapse-vscode:v2.0.6```

## Usage
The optimal experience is achieved when used in conjunction with the [Dev Container](https://code.visualstudio.com/docs/devcontainers/containers#_creating-a-devcontainerjson-file).

### 1. Download the sample

```
The folder structure:
├── .devcontainer # Root folder for Dev Container configuration
│   ├── devcontainer.json # Configuration file for VSCode Dev Container
│   ├── docker-compose.yaml # Docker Compose file for container orchestration
│   └── mariner
│       └── Dockerfile # Custom Dockerfile
```

[Container Image for Synapse VS Code Sample](https://github.com/microsoft/SynapseVSCode/tree/main/samples/.devcontainer)

### 2. Requirements
- Install [Docker Desktop](https://www.docker.com/products/docker-desktop/)
- Install [Visual Studio Code](https://code.visualstudio.com/download)
- Install the [VS Code Remote Development pack](https://marketplace.visualstudio.com/items?itemName=ms-vscode-remote.vscode-remote-extensionpack)
- Requires the following environment flags
  "ACCEPT_EULA=Y"

### 3. VS Code command palette
Open the [VS Code command palette](https://code.visualstudio.com/docs/getstarted/userinterface#_command-palette) and select/type 'Reopen in Container'
